findings.premise: The design covers S003's atomic replay, lifecycle protection and storage-isolation acceptance criteria without introducing a reset implementation.
findings.evidence: DEF §6.3 requires complete-or-prior commits, replay-safe revision/deletion boundaries, and independent memory/index reset or rebuild. The LLD designs atomic effects/receipt/generation, persistent broad-forget barriers, stale-read rejection and isolation tests. It explicitly retains S003's acceptance responsibility while identifying S7/S9-dependent cleanup evidence as pending. The actual Indexer.fullIndex path calls deleteEntitiesForRepo, which deletes graph entities and repository vectors; the proposed rebuild test therefore targets a real destructive index path. findings.premise: The existing runtime can compose queue and store participants in the stated shutdown order without an algorithm change.
findings.evidence: EmbeddedMemoryService stops every participant, serially executes 'for (const work of this.#work) await work.drain()', waits for model settlement, then attempts each quiescent participant's close in array order. Any close failure prevents owner.close. The existing multi-participant test verifies all releases are attempted after a close failure and ownership remains held. This supports the proposed [queue, storeOwnedWork] composition; drain failures deliberately retain ownership without proceeding to resource closure. [files: packages/project-memory/src/runtime.ts, packages/project-memory/src/host-node.ts, packages/project-memory/src/__tests__/runtime.test.ts]
findings.action: Add the proposed queue-proof/native-work integration cases to establish that the new adapter satisfies this existing contract.

findings.premise: The recorded Lance probe establishes basic SDK compatibility rather than crash or cross-platform durability.
findings.evidence: qualification-probe.json records Node 22.23.2 on darwin, one merge-version increment, nullable scalar vectors, pinned-reader behavior and normal reopen. lance-probe.mjs performs those assertions and closes normally; it contains no SIGKILL or Linux qualification. Its explicit limit is 'No crash/fsync, Linux, concurrent-reader-under-kill or power-loss qualification'. Installed 0.40.0 declarations also expose checkout, checkoutLatest, mergeInsert and orderBy, consistent with the documented [Table API](https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/classes/Table/). findings.premise: The dedicated authoritative store is new, while the receipt-verifier integration port already exists with the stated proof fields.
findings.evidence: The package currently composes FileQueue without a store. ReceiptVerifier already provides byIdentity, byOperation and optional confirmRetirement; TerminalProof includes operationId, identityDigest, payloadHash, scope, scopeEpoch, generation, receipt and queueTerminal. FileQueue accepts the verifier as its fifth constructor argument and uses it for retry reconciliation and acknowledgement. Existing backend Lance access is a PATHS-bound singleton with backend ownership dependencies, supporting the choice to create a separate package-owned connection. findings.premise: The persisted embedding compatibility metadata covers the normalization version required upstream.
findings.evidence: Requirements L-05 says 'Persist embedding model identity, dimension and normalization version.' The strict root payload and initialization marker in LLD §3.11 contain embeddingModel and embeddingDimension but no embedding-normalization version or defined equivalent. ProcessingVersion.normalizer describes per-revision processing and may be null for deterministic operations; the design never binds it to embedding preprocessing or checks it at store reopen. The existing ModelPort likewise exposes only model and dimension, so this requirement is not supplied implicitly by a consumed contract. findings.premise: The proposed policy-only wrapper can preserve INVALID_REQUEST and historical REVISION_CONFLICT through unchanged QueueAdmission.
findings.evidence: QueueAdmission.append catches errors from '#policy.admit' and passes them to policyFailure. That helper preserves only UNBOUND_PROJECT and POLICY_DENIED; every other error becomes NOT_READY. A no-I/O execution of the real QueueAdmission with a minimal queue stub confirmed 'INVALID_REQUEST -> NOT_READY' and 'REVISION_CONFLICT -> NOT_READY'. Therefore the wrapper placement specified in §3.16 cannot deliver its promised forged-payload INVALID_REQUEST or policy-originated historical conflict while QueueAdmission remains unchanged. POLICY_DENIED does survive. findings.action: Correct the admission/error-boundary design and change inventory so module validation errors and historical conflicts reach callers with the specified codes, while retaining sanitization of host-policy failures. Add end-to-end public-submit assertions for both codes and unchanged queue bytes.

findings.premise: Receipt verification distinguishes unavailable proof from absence and prevents acknowledgement or retirement without matching authoritative proof.
findings.evidence: readReceipt converts thrown, malformed and explicit unavailable results into ReceiptUnavailableError. matchProof checks operation, identity, payload, scope, epoch, event and optional generation. FileQueue.markResolved requires a found matching proof before terminal checkpoint publication; retirement additionally confirms retained digest references before unlink. These real callers support the LLD's proof-preserving failure handling and store-before-queue-close dependency. [files: packages/project-memory/src/queue/receipts.ts, packages/project-memory/src/queue/file-queue.ts, packages/project-memory/src/queue/retirement.ts]
findings.action: Ensure the S3 adapter preserves these distinctions during fencing, draining and reopen.
